pr.title: Use an interpreter in MIR jump threading
pr.description: This allows to understand assignments of aggregate constants. This case appears more frequently with GVN promoting aggregates to constants.
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: This PR is a pure JumpThreading optimization enhancement, not a semantic bug fix. The pre-change pass simply failed to register a threading opportunity for aggregate constants, leaving `switchInt(move _5) -> [0: bb2, otherwise: bb1]` in place; the post-change pass evaluates the aggregate constant and replaces the switch with `goto -> bb2`. For the added regression test `const FOO: (u8, u8) = (5, 13); let (a, b) = FOO; if a == 7 { b } else { a }`, `a == 7` is false, so the original switch takes `bb2` and returns `a = 5`, while the threaded `goto -> bb2` also executes `_0 = _2` and returns `a = 5`. Both revisions are observationally identical for every defined input (the function ignores its `x` parameter). The "historical incomplete transformation" is only a missed optimization opportunity, not an incorrect value transformation, so there is no source-grounded original/transformed pair that produces differing defined results. Manufacturing a difference by changing the compared constant, collapsing the return slot incorrectly, or introducing an unrelated miscompile would not be justified by this PR.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, jump threading handled constants through `Operand::Constant` only by direct scalar extraction: `let constant = constant.const_.normalize(self.tcx, self.param_env).try_to_scalar_int()?; conditions.iter_matches(constant).for_each(register_opportunity);`. Thus a value assigned from an aggregate constant (e.g. a tuple constant destructured into fields) could not be resolved element-by-element, so conditions on projections of that aggregate were not tied to the switch target.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incomplete transformation failed to register a threading opportunity when the compared value originated from a projection of an aggregate constant. For `const FOO: (u8, u8) = (5, 13); let (a, b) = FOO; if a == 7 { b } else { a }`, the pre-change MIR kept `_4 = const _; _2 = (_4.0: u8); _5 = Eq(move _6, const 7_u8); switchInt(move _5) -> [0: bb2, otherwise: bb1];`, whereas the intended transformed output threads to `goto -> bb2;`. The fix evaluates aggregate constants with an interpreter and walks projected values (`Field`, `Variant`, `Discriminant`, `DerefLen`) so each tracked place is matched against the constant.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions where a value compared against a scalar constant is obtained by reading fields/variants/discriminants/pointer lengths from a constant aggregate (tuple, array, ADT, enum, references), typically after `let` destructuring of a `const` aggregate and especially common when GVN promotes aggregates to constants.
analysis.trigger: An `Assign` from `Operand::Constant` whose constant is an aggregate (not a plain scalar), followed by projections into that place and a comparison that value_analysis has recorded as a condition leading to a switch target.
preconditions: The value_analysis Map can find the assigned place/projection (`self.map.find`/`try_get_idx`).
The aggregate constant can be interpreted with `self.ecx.eval_mir_constant(&constant.const_, None, None)` using the pass's InterpCx over `DummyMachine` and the same param_env.

Each projection element is resolvable: `TrackElem::Field` via `project_field`, `TrackElem::Variant` via `project_downcast`, `TrackElem::Discriminant` via `read_discriminant`/`discriminant_for_variant`, `TrackElem::DerefLen` via `deref_pointer`/`len`.
The projected immediate is `Immediate::Scalar(Scalar::Int(int))`, since only integer scalars are matched with `iter_matches`.
Layouts must be obtainable through the interpreter (`self.ecx.layout_of(...)`) rather than only `tcx.layout_of(param_env.and(ty))`.
pitfalls: Do not thread through a `SetDiscriminant` that may be a no-op for the untagged variant of a niche encoding; the code checks `writes_discriminant` and skips when `*variant_index == untagged_variant`.
Unions are deliberately unsupported: `AggregateKind::Adt(.., Some(_)) => return None`.
Enum aggregates must apply `TrackElem::Variant(*variant_index)` after handling the discriminant, otherwise field projections are attached to the wrong place.
Only integer scalar immediates can be matched; non-integer or non-scalar immediates simply yield no opportunity.
The interpreter must be constructed with the pass param_env and `DummyMachine`; using an unrelated evaluation context could disagree with layout/discriminant computations.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a mir-opt regression test `aggregate` in `tests/mir-opt/jump_threading.rs` with `const FOO: (u8, u8) = (5, 13); let (a, b) = FOO; if a == 7 { b } else { a }`, assert `// CHECK-LABEL: fn aggregate(` and `// CHECK-NOT: switchInt(`, register `// EMIT_MIR jump_threading.aggregate.JumpThreading.diff`, and validate both `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind` revisions show the switch replaced by a direct `goto -> bb2;`. Also keep the existing mir-opt cases intact and ensure `fn main` has the label check.
analysis.summary: JumpThreading was extended to use an interpreter so aggregate constants (tuples/ADTs/enums) can be projected and matched against tracked conditions. Previously only scalar constants could seed threading opportunities, so destructuring a constant aggregate and comparing one field left the `switchInt` unthreaded.
evidence: This allows to understand assignments of aggregate constants. This case appears more frequently with GVN promoting aggregates to constants.
